title: Man. Post. Cap. X: GAR — even if the ban lasts, nature’s covenant is prior to grace
pass_a_gloss: Garissoles meets the ceremonial-abrogate objection: even if the paradise ban remained, Placeus says it is abolished for us like legal ceremonies, since breach of a ceremonial law cannot be imputed when we are not under it. Reply: the redeemed are freed from that primal ban’s rigor as from ceremonial laws, so its threats do not look to them. Yet nature is prior to grace—grace comes upon nature and reforms and restores it—and each is first a human before a believer or Christian. So nature’s status and the natural law or covenant are prior to the covenant of grace; each is considered first under the natural covenant before the gracious. Therefore that we are already not under that law ought to have been proved, not merely supposed.
pass_b_english: GAR. Next it is opposed that even if that law remained, it has nonetheless been abolished with respect to us, as the legal ceremonies, since it was a ceremonial law, whose violation cannot be imputed to us because we are not under that law—just as violation of the ceremonial laws cannot be imputed to us because we do not live under those laws.

Reply 1. Those who have been redeemed through Christ, and are sharers in that redemption, have indeed been freed, as from the ceremonial laws, so also from the rigor of this primitive law, and so the threats added to it do not look to them.

But still, as nature is prior to grace (since grace comes upon nature and reforms and restores it), and each one is conceived to be a human before he is a believer or a Christian: so also the status of nature, and the law or Natural covenant, is prior to the covenant of Grace, and so each one is considered first under the natural covenant, before under the gracious.
Therefore it ought not to have been supposed, but proved, that we are already not under that law.
source_text: GAR. Deinde opponitur, etiamsi lex illa permaneret, tamen abolitam esse respectu nostri, ut legales ceremonias, cum fuerit lex ceremonialis, cuius violatio non potest nobis imputari, quia non sumus sub ea lege; sicut violatio legum ceremonialium non potest nobis imputari, quia sub iis legibus non agimus. Resp. 1. Qui per Christum redempti sunt, & redemptionis illius participes, ii sane, ut a legibus ceremonialibus, ita etiam ab huius legis primitivae rigore liberati sunt, adeoque ad eos non spectant comminationes illi additae. Sed tamen, ut natura prior est gratiae (cum gratia naturae superveniat, eamque reformet & instaurat), & unusquisque concipitur prius esse homo, quam sit fidelis aut Christianus: Ita etiam status naturae, & lex sive foedus Naturale prius est foedere Gratiae, adeoque unusquisque consideratur prius sub foedere naturali, quam sub gratuito. Quare non debuit supponi, sed probari nos iam non esse sub ea lege.

choices.choice: Natural covenant prior to grace; prove we left the ban
